rounds.text: JLA Infraville Shoppers Ltd trades at a steep discount with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.22x, based on a share price of ₹ 2.60 against a book value of ₹ 11.8 [E1]. This deep value is further highlighted by a tiny micro-cap market capitalisation of ₹ 1.69 Cr [E2]. Furthermore, the stock rests near the absolute bottom of its annual spectrum, sitting only 2% of the way up its 52-week range between a low of 2 and a high of 8 [E4]. Supporting the bull case, the screen reason indicates that earnings growth is accelerating [E46]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E3].

The fundamental operating engine of this business is actively destroying capital, evidenced by a negative return on capital employed of -1.4% and a negative return on equity of -2.0% [E5, E6]. This operational decay has culminated in a catastrophic collapse in trailing twelve-month profit growth of -291% [E8]. Compounded profit growth over the last decade has stagnated at a negligible 2%, demonstrating a persistent inability to generate long-term earnings expansion [E7]. Market expectations have become completely disconnected from underlying reality, with recent price growth outpacing profit growth by 231% even as profitability craters [E37]. Furthermore, shareholders receive zero income return from their investment, as the dividend yield sits firmly at 0.00% [E3]. Conceded: the low price-to-book ratio of 0.22x and the screen reason noting accelerating earnings growth [E1, E46].

Conceded: negative returns on capital and equity [E5, E6], the stagnation of ten-year compounded profit growth at two percent [E7], the severe trailing profit contraction [E8], the total lack of dividend income [E3], and the divergence between recent price growth and earnings delivery [E37]. However, the market has pushed this micro-cap down to sit merely two percent up from its absolute yearly low [E4], creating an extreme pricing dislocation relative to the underlying assets. This excessive pessimism ignores the fundamental margin of safety provided by a price-to-book ratio of just 0.22x, meaning the stock trades at less than a quarter of its recorded book value of ₹11.8 per share against a market price of ₹2.60 [E1, E2]. Furthermore, quantitative screening explicitly detects that earnings growth is accelerating [E46], signaling a structural inflection that the backward-looking trailing metrics fail to capture.

Conceded: the price-to-book ratio is 0.22x with a share price of ₹ 2.60 against a book value of ₹ 11.8 [E1] and the stock sits at 2% of its 52-week range [E4]. However, trading at a steep discount to book value does not constitute a margin of safety when capital allocation destroys value, evidenced by a negative ROCE of -1.4% and an ROE of -2.0% [E5, E6]. The claim of a structural earnings inflection via screening [E46] is directly contradicted by the company's severe trailing profit contraction of -291% and meager ten-year compounded profit growth of just 2% [E7, E8]. Furthermore, price growth already outpaces profit growth by 231%, proving that market expectations are running well ahead of actual delivery rather than ignoring a turnaround [E37]. Finally, the micro-cap status with a market capitalization of ₹ 1.69 Cr and zero dividend yield offers no cash return to patient holders while operational erosion persists [E2, E3].
